elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1 requires "at least ninety (90) days' written notice", three times the preferred 30-day maximum.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither the rendered 11.1 nor any other rendered text contains any refund of prepaid fees, pro rata or otherwise; instead Customer pays a fee on exit.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Rendered 10.2 now reads "M&I may, effective only at the end of the then-current Term, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services)", so no mid-term Vendor convenience withdrawal remains; the surviving immediate right is condition-based ("upon any final regulatory, legislative, or judicial" determination), not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — within the 60–90 day band and at the outer, not exceeded, edge.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: fee "in an amount not to exceed three (3) months' Fees", and the additional uncapped charge ("any unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses...") is deleted, so no residual exit charge can push the total above the cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Rendered 10.2 expressly ties the effective date to term end: "effective only at the end of the then-current Term".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Already met and retained in 10.2: "upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer".

reasons: Fallback level is complete on all four elements: Customer notice cut from one year to ninety (90) days, the Termination for Convenience Fee capped at three (3) months' Fees, M&I's non-Core withdrawal right expressly made effective only at the end of the then-current Term, and M&I's existing ninety (90) days' notice retained.

Preferred level fails on two elements and should not be claimed: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees anywhere in the rendered text. Targeting the fallback is therefore the correct level.

Minimality holds. Deletion of the "In addition to the foregoing... any unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses" pass-through is necessary to the fee-cap element, since an uncapped parallel exit charge would let the total early-termination cost exceed three months' Fees. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories or other extras were added, and the favourable retained language (Event of Default / Section 11.3 carve-outs, the 50/50 payment timing, Section 13.4 carve-out) was left untouched.

Intent is preserved: the 50/50 payment mechanic, the carve-outs for Events of Default and Section 11.3, the Section 13.4 carve-out, and M&I's condition-based immediate regulatory termination all survive without contradiction. The "Estimated Remaining Value" definition (p0039) was correctly left intact rather than deleted; drafter should confirm it is still cross-referenced elsewhere in the Agreement so it is not orphaned, but an unused definition creates no dangling reference in the edited clauses.

Classification as a deviation is correct: the original required a full year's notice plus a fee measured on all remaining months of an eight-year Term (plus uncapped Conversion costs and Expenses), and gave M&I an "at any time" mid-term withdrawal right — failures of the fallback on both notice and fee, and on Vendor mid-term convenience.
Severity remains high: the underlying clause was in walk-away territory (no usable Customer exit in a multi-year term, mid-term Vendor withdrawal), and the redline brings it only to the fallback.
